messages:
elaine_customer: Hi team — after we cut the new Go SDK release tagged v2.0.0 customers are seeing build failures. Example error from a downstream repo:

elaine_customer: ```
$ go build ./...
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.0.0: module declares its path (github.com/redwood/inference-go) at revision v2.0.0, but was required as github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2
```

alice_support: Sorry you're hitting that, can you paste the minimal repro (consumer go.mod + your SDK go.mod + go env)?

elaine_customer: Repro attached — consumer is importing with the /v2 path (we updated imports to github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2). Our SDK repo go.mod currently is: 

elaine_customer: ```
module github.com/redwood/inference-go

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/some/dependency v1.2.3
)
```

elaine_customer: go env/goversion:
```
go version go1.20 linux/amd64
GO111MODULE=on
```

ben_engineer: Root cause: the module was tagged v2 but the module path in go.mod wasn't bumped to include /v2. For semver v2+ Go modules must declare module .../v2 if you want to publish a major v2 tag that consumers import as /v2. Because we tagged v2.0.0 without updating the module path, consumers who import github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 hit that exact error.

ben_engineer: Short-term workarounds for consumers:
- Add a replace in the consumer's go.mod to remap the /v2 import to the published module: 
```
replace github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 => github.com/redwood/inference-go v2.0.0
```
This forces the toolchain to use the existing module that doesn't declare /v2.

- Or pin to the v1.x line until we publish a corrected v2.0.1: `go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v1.9.3`

ben_engineer: Long-term fix (recommended): update the SDK's go.mod to `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2`, cut a new tag v2.0.1 (or v2.0.0+fix) and push tags. Steps we plan to do: 
```bash
# on release branch
git checkout -b release/v2-path-fix
git apply <<'PATCH'
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: go.mod
@@
-module github.com/redwood/inference-go
+module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2
*** End Patch
PATCH
# commit & tag
git commit -am "module: add /v2 path for v2 release"
git tag v2.0.1
git push origin release/v2-path-fix
git push origin v2.0.1
```

ci-bot: CI failures repro in our release pipeline: 
```
--- FAIL: go mod download
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.0.0: module declares its path (github.com/redwood/inference-go) at revision v2.0.0, but was required as github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2
exit status 1
```

dave_release: Thanks — we'll cut v2.0.1 with the module path fix today. Ben, can you open the PR with the minimal go.mod change + release note that explains the import-path change? I'll coordinate the tag and announce rollback guidance.

ben_engineer: On it — I'll include migration notes for consumers: 
- If you import /v2, update to v2.0.1 once available.
- Temporary replace shown above works until the new tag propagates.

alice_support: Elaine — tl;dr for now: either add the replace to your consumers' go.mod or pin to the v1 branch. We'll notify you when v2.0.1 is pushed. Sorry for the disruption :disappointed: 

elaine_customer: Appreciate the quick response. We'll add the replace in CI for now and watch for the v2.0.1 tag. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
